hosting.//: The main shell — malvinai.com / app.malvinai.com. Serves the exact same Vite build as the 'stores' target below (one `npm run build`, deployed to both — see README/deploy notes); the two only differ in which domain they're attached to and their headers. Nothing should ever frame THIS target, hence frame-ancestors 'none' + X-Frame-Options DENY stay strict here.

headers.//: The beta Android APK (place app-release.apk at dist/downloads/malvinai-beta.apk before deploying, matching ANDROID_APK_URL in src/config/appDistribution.ts). Chrome needs Content-Disposition: attachment, not just a Content-Type, to reliably download-to-disk rather than try to navigate to it as a page — .apk has no in-browser renderer, so without this the behavior varies by device.

Content-hashed build output (dist/assets/*-HASH.js, *-HASH.css) — the filename itself changes whenever the content does, so it's always safe to cache these as long as possible. This is the standard Vite/SPA caching split: never cache the HTML shell, cache everything it references forever.

index.html (and any other non-hashed root file the ** rewrite serves) must NEVER be cached — it's what names the current build's asset hashes. Without this, Firebase Hosting's default caching could keep serving an old index.html (pointing at JS chunks a NEW deploy already deleted) for up to an hour after a deploy, which is exactly the "Failed to load module script... text/html" MIME error from stale asset URLs 404'ing and falling through to the SPA rewrite.

Service workers must be re-fetched on every load to pick up updates promptly — browsers already re-check these more than normal assets, but explicit no-cache removes any ambiguity from CDN-level caching in between.

frame-src now includes the stores target's origin so StoreFront.tsx's <iframe> is actually allowed to load it — 'self' alone doesn't cover a different subdomain. script-src gained www.gstatic.com: firebase-messaging-sw.js's importScripts() call to it was being silently blocked by this SAME header (a service worker with no CSP of its own inherits the registering page's CSP), which is why background push notifications never fired once someone added this to their Home Screen — the fix in index.html's <meta> CSP alone wasn't enough, this header applies in addition to it.

hosting.//: Merchant storefronts / QR destinations — stores.malvinai.com. Same build as 'app' above, deployed separately so it can carry DIFFERENT framing headers: this is the one target that's allowed to be embedded, and only by the app target's own origin(s) (see StoreFront.tsx for why real origin separation is what makes its <iframe> sandbox safe without allow-same-origin). X-Frame-Options is deliberately omitted here — it can't express 'allow this specific other origin', only ALLOW-FROM (unsupported in modern Chrome/Firefox) or DENY/SAMEORIGIN, so frame-ancestors alone is what gates this.
